newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Nov COB electricity ends higher, Nov PV flat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Nov COB electricity ends higher, Nov PV flat.

text.p: NYMEX California-Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures settled higher Wednesday, while November Palo Verde futures finished unchanged amid mixed trading of the bulk power in the western U.S.
Daily cash prices in the Northwest were mostly lower from Tuesday's levels, and in the Southwest a tad stronger despite modest weather-related demand in the West, market sources said.
Peak, firm spot power at the California-Oregon Border (COB) for Thursday was quoted at $18.50-$19.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), and at Palo Verde (PV) $21.00-$22.00.
Power supplies to the Southwest were expected to be further reduced into mid-October because of maintenance and flow testing on the Pacific Intertie.
The line, which carries cheap hydroelectricity to the Southwest from the Northwest, has been derated since a major power outage in the West in August.

Bonneville Power Administration, which operates part of the intertie, said capacity on the direct current (DC) portion of the line would be cut until Oct 20, at times to zero, and the alternate current (AC) part as low as 2,000.
The DC and AC portions of the intertie have maximum capacities of 3,200 MW and 4,800 MW.
Participants were not certain how a further reduction in capacity would affect spot power supplies during a low demand period.
November COB futures finished at $17.60, up nine cents after being traded between $17.40 and $17.65. December COB ended up 18 cents at $18.80.
November PV futures settled at $16.60, unchanged from Tuesday. December PV also closed flat at $17.35.
Despite today's mixed close, most participants expected the market to test the upper end of the complex's recent trading range.
"We're still in an uptrend," said one Northwest trader.
NYMEX estimated 191 COB and 115 PV contracts changed hands Wednesday.
